top_choice_rationale: P003 rewards a verified discovery of a new class of electronic matter: Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling alone gives a Z2 insulator with protected helical edge states, and Molenkamp's group measured the edge conductance in HgTe within a year. Over fifteen years of replication, ARPES links between calculated and measured band structure, and a lasting change in how materials are searched make it mature. I accept that credit is a compromise (Bernevig, Hughes and the 3D topological insulator contributors are left out) and that the citation is compound, but the physics is solid. P001 is a close second: a mature, reproduced, cleanly two-named instrument-enabling advance, though it overlaps the 2005 and 2012 prizes and is closer to measurement capability than to a surprise about nature. P002 is a real and consequential discovery, but I defer on particle physics and the three-person credit from large collaborations is hard to document. No award is the least preferred, because several candidates are scientifically mature.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; P003 is a condensed-matter topic close to my own field but I have no stated personal connection to Kane, Mele or Molenkamp
